data.decision:
Operator 2026-10-02 (research R-task-time): the review budget is part of ddflow's workflow, not agent-instruction prose. (1) [review].max_rounds (default 2; 0 = unlimited) bounds FULL review rounds per gate per item; counted from the gate's review records on the item; starting another full round beyond the budget is refused with exit 3 naming the alternatives (a delta review of the fix commits, `ddflow review triage` of the remaining findings, --force --reason); [review].on_exceed = refuse|warn (default refuse for full rounds; a delta review and triage are never refused). (2) A review of a gate that already has a recorded review defaults to a DELTA of the commits since the last reviewed head (evidence records the reviewed head), merging coverage into the gate record like --chunk does; `--full` forces a full round (counts against the budget). (3) `ddflow review <id> --gate rubber_duck,critic` (or --gate all) runs the reviewer gates concurrently (CLI and MCP), because they review the same diff. (4) Convergence is shown: `gate status` and `brief` say 'critic round 2/2, findings: N untriaged, M confirmed HIGH/MEDIUM' and 'review converged: yes/no' (yes = every finding triaged and no confirmed HIGH/MEDIUM defect left); `complete`/merge print a NOTE when not converged and never block (D-failed-critic-not-blocking stands). (5) [review].time_budget_s (default 900) bounds one review run: chunks not reviewed in time make the run `partial` with what was reviewed, never a hang. (6) Lease hold visibility: while an item holds contended globs (other agents waiting, claim-fairness registry) and is only running review gates, brief and doctor say so with the hold time and [lease].hold_warn_s (default 1800) warns the holder; a warning, never an eviction. (7) The shared agent-instruction text on review rounds is replaced by the shipped driver docs describing these features. Defaults are revisitable; none of it blocks completion.

AMENDED 2026-10-17 (roadmap review contradictions; supersedes D-review-budget): WHAT CHANGED: (4) 'complete/merge print a NOTE when not converged and never block (D-failed-critic-not-blocking stands)' is replaced by: 'converged' is the predicate of D-failed-review-gate (every confirmed finding is followed by a later delta round that did not re-raise it; an all-refuted triage passes); not converged means merge and complete refuse (exit 3) unless the operator overrides with a recorded reason, and the NOTE explains the refusal; only the unreviewed-chunks `partial` of (5) stays non-blocking. (1) The round budget counts FULL rounds only; fix rounds are free ([review].fix_round_free, D-failed-review-gate). (2) A delta re-review also receives the prior findings with their triage and checks each cited location against the new code (D-gate-economy-r3 (d)). The closing 'none of it blocks completion' no longer holds for (4).

data.decision:
Operator 2026-10-03 (verbatim): 'Do show who is locking a file, but also put a limit on the lock in terms of time so if the lock lasts too long we allow someone else to edit the file and then correct the issues at merge, and in case there are merge issues the unit tests shall be run to verify the merging correction didn't create own bugs and recessions. All of this behavior should be configurable, including timeout, unlocking, via config, cli or mcp.' Chosen over the two options in the earlier analysis (visibility OR early release): BOTH. (1) Visibility: who holds which file, since when, who waits (B-lease-hold-visibility). (2) A time limit on a hold: [lease].hold_max_s (default 3600; 0 = never, the old behaviour). After that age a lease on CONTENDED globs (someone waits or claims) becomes BREAKABLE: another agent's claim of an overlapping item is allowed, recorded as a lease.overlap (holder, claimant, files, age) and shown in both agents' briefs; the original holder is never evicted or deleted, it keeps its worktree and branch. (3) Reconciliation at merge: the first branch to merge wins the file; the second merges main in; if that merge conflicts, or both touched the same file, ddflow records merge.reconciled with the files, REFUSES to complete until the full unit suite (and the slow scenarios when their path is touched) has run on the reconciled tree and passed, and the gate evidence names the reconciled files and the suite run. Reconciliation can never be skipped silently (--force --reason is the recorded exception). (4) All configurable: [lease].hold_max_s, [lease].break_on_timeout (default true), [lease].hold_warn_s, [lease].reconcile_tests (default full; full|affected|off); CLI `ddflow config lease.hold_max_s N [--local]`, `ddflow lease break <item> --reason` / `ddflow lease keep <item> --for N` (operator can unlock early or extend), MCP ddflow_configure for the knobs and the break/keep actions (agents may extend only their own hold; breaking another's is operator or timeout only). Defaults are the shipped defaults for every project. Risks accepted and mitigations: two branches edit one file -> textual conflicts are caught by git, semantic conflicts by the mandatory post-reconcile suite; never evict a live holder; a break is a visible event, never silent.

AMENDED 2026-10-17 (roadmap review contradictions; supersedes D-lease-hold-limit): WHAT CHANGED in (4) and (2): [lease].break_on_timeout defaults to FALSE (D-lease-break-explicit, operator 2026-10-17 review): an idle contended lease is broken by the explicit act `ddflow claim --break` (operator or agent, recorded as lease.expired; the holder keeps its worktree and branch); the automatic break happens only when a project sets break_on_timeout = true. [lease].reconcile_tests defaults to 'affected' (D-gate-economy-r3): the reconcile-at-merge step is KEPT (merge.reconciled is recorded and complete is refused until the affected tests have passed on the reconciled tree), and the FULL suite runs per batch in the merge-queue integrator. Where this text says 'default true' for break_on_timeout or 'default full' for reconcile_tests, read false and affected. Order of resolution when items collide: see D-lock-cycle-selfheal-r2.

Operator 2026-10-15, verbatim: 'Can you have those DX set for implementation next after the bug fixes and with priority over the other tasks? Can you set the rules, and also can you make sure that ddflow if it detects circular dependency or blockage which was undetected and not prevented in advance should refill the tasks with dependency on each other in order to prevent circular waiting and dependency and this way to force unblock?'. (1) PRIORITY: the locking and ordering features come right after the bug fixes and ahead of every other feature: DX-pins-regenerate, DX-no-hold-and-wait and DX-conflict-autoorder (priority 1), then DX-lease-progress-breakable, DX-lease-wait-cycle and DX-merge-queue (2), then the other DX tasks. (2) PREVENT IN ADVANCE: pin files are regenerated, not leased (DX-pins-regenerate, DX-merge-queue); a lease is never widened by hold-and-wait (DX-no-hold-and-wait); a contended lease without progress is breakable (DX-lease-progress-breakable, D-lease-hold-limit); a task that adds a knob, event kind or command declares the pin files it will touch up front. (3) DETECT: a cycle in the wait-for graph, or a wait older than a limit with nothing running, is reported by doctor, status, brief and the lanes advisor (DX-lease-wait-cycle). (4) SELF-HEAL, the new rule: when ddflow detects a circular dependency or blockage that was NOT declared and NOT prevented in advance, ddflow itself ADDS `needs` edges between the colliding items, in a deterministic order (priority, then progress, then claim time, then id), never an edge that closes a cycle, so the circular waiting cannot recur and the unblock is forced; the later item yields the contested globs and waits for the earlier one. Every edge is a logged event by actor ddflow:auto-order with the evidence, visible in brief and doctor and reversible with ddflow update --needs; [schedule].auto_order = off | propose | apply (default apply for a detected cycle or an over-limit wait, propose for repeated collisions); a repeated collision of the same pair makes the edge permanent in the plan (DX-conflict-autoorder). (5) AGENTS: never poll-wait in a private loop; use ddflow wait or report to the coordinator; do not hold a lease while waiting for another (release or yield on request); when ddflow tells you to yield, do so at the next safe point. Users and companies can change every limit and the mode (r-company-workflows).

(3) An AUTOMATIC break happens only when [lease].break_on_timeout = true, which is not the default. Globs repaired: the services are packages where noted.

data.decision:
A scheduled job is a first-class definition (schedule record) whose DUE state ddflow computes from the log (calendar days, done tasks, done phases, upstream needs, missed policy). [D-skills-spec-native] A ddflow-managed skill is a spec-compliant directory (SKILL.md + optional scripts/ references/ assets/) that any agent reads unchanged. ddflow-specific data (digest, source, version, sync state) lives in the event log and .ddflow/skills.lock, or in the spec's free-form metadata map, never in new frontmatter fields.

[D-skills-canonical-store] Default canonical store is .agents/skills/ (the cross-client convention); [skills].canonical can name another. 'ddflow skill sync' makes symlinks (default), copies, or generated files in each enabled agent's directory, marks what it manages, never overwrites a skill it did not create, and reports drift. Skills already in an agent directory are adopted, not moved, until the operator asks.

[D-skills-operator-answers] Decided by the operator 2026-10-03: (1) YAML parsing uses PyYAML with a colon-quote retry (add it as a dependency). (2) Skill sync defaults to COPY with drift detection against a managed sidecar; symlink is opt-in. (3) Install/pin use skills-lock.json at the repo root, compatible with the vercel format, with ddflow-namespaced fields (ref, commit, treeSha, hashAlgo, files) and a precisely defined full sha256 tree digest. (4) skill doctor: errors fail the exit code (1), warnings are advisory, and the report always says static checks only. What the coordinator did by hand on 2026-10-15: notice that an agent had been idle for an hour holding shared files (events stopped, only heartbeats), stop and replace it, resume stopped agents when their blocker merged, tell waiting agents the merge order, and relaunch finishers. In advise mode it only reports. Regression tests with fake lanes: an idle holder with a waiter is reported and then taken over only when policy allows; a stopped lane with a ready blocker is flagged RESUME; the merge order follows the queue.

(The ladder stays: nudge -> ask status -> request yield -> park -> take over/relaunch -> escalate, mode off|advise|act.)

--- ORIGINAL TEXT (where it conflicts with the note above, the note governs) ---
Operator 2026-10-15, verbatim: 'Can you also make ddflow to periodically inspect agents and subagents for if they have stalled or locked so it can detect fast situations like these or crashes and to try to correct them'. Today stalls are found only when a person or the coordinator happens to look: on 2026-10-15 one agent sat idle for an hour with a current lease (a heartbeat loop kept renewing it), three agents deadlocked for 45+ minutes, a wait loop timed out unnoticed, and a stopped agent was found by reading event timestamps by hand. Build a WATCHDOG: (1) WHAT IT INSPECTS, per lane (every lease holder, agent and subagent, in the lane ledger): STALLED = no progress for [watch].stall_s while its lease is renewed (progress = the watermark of DX-lease-progress-breakable: the last event that is not a lease renewal, plus commits in its worktree and test jobs in flight); IDLE-HEARTBEAT = renewals continue but nothing else for [watch].idle_s; LOCKED = it is in a cycle of the wait-for graph or waits on a lease held by a stalled lane (DX-lease-wait-cycle); CRASHED = the holder's process or session is gone (lease heartbeats carry pid, host and session id so a dead process is seen in minutes, not after the 30-minute TTL), or its lease expired with work attached; RUNAWAY = the same gate failed N times, the same command repeated, a job over its budget, or a review round loop; UNRESPONSIVE = a nudge or yield request went unanswered for [watch].reply_s; STARVED = context or quota pressure from the governor (P-governor sampling) so the lane cannot continue; and every found condition is a finding with evidence. (2) WHEN, without a daemon (D-sched-no-daemon, amended by D-daemons): opportunistically on every ddflow call, throttled by [watch].interval_s (a cheap check against the last-inspected marker, using the already folded state); in the hook rungs (SessionStart, Stop, SubagentStop, UserPromptSubmit) so the master session sees findings; as a scheduler job (P-schedule due/executor-basic) for headless projects; and, when the operator enables the managed lane-supervisor/scheduler daemon kind (D-daemons), on its tick. (3) CORRECT, as a ladder with a mode per step ([watch].act = off | advise | act, default advise, per finding kind): nudge the lane (a note or message it reads at its next call, P-context-sync.tell / P-spawn.steer); ask for status; request yield of contested globs; PARK the lane (DX-park-and-resume) so its work is kept; take over or relaunch from the worktree (DX-dispatch-supervise); add the ordering edges that stop a recurrence (DX-conflict-autoorder); escalate to the operator with the exact commands. Never discards work, never acts on a lane with progress, every step is a logged event (actor ddflow:watchdog) with its evidence and is reversible. (4) SURFACES: `ddflow watch inspect|status|history|ack` on CLI, MCP and the plain prompt ('is anything stuck?'), a one-line summary in brief, status and the statusline, doctor findings, and the dispatcher plan (DX-dispatch-plan) consumes the same findings so a stalled lane's slot is refilled. (5) Reuse: P-observe.detectors (deterministic detector registry: lock contention, rework loops), the lanes ledger and advisor (`ddflow lanes advise`), the jobs engine for hung test jobs, DX-doctor-ack for acknowledged findings. Regression tests with fake lanes and a fake clock: an idle-heartbeat lane is STALLED after the limit and an active one never; a dead pid is CRASHED within [watch].crash_s; a three-lane crossing-glob case is LOCKED and the ladder escalates step by step; advise mode writes only findings; act mode parks the stalled lane and keeps its worktree; findings are deduplicated and rate-limited. (1) Every renamed or removed CLI command, flag, MCP tool, tool argument and config key keeps working through a declared alias with a one-line deprecation notice until ddflow 1.0 (hidden from help and tools/list, never removed before 1.0); ddflow upgrade rewrites ddflow-managed references to the new names; releases are versioned by impact (a declared breaking change is a minor bump while 0.x), not patch-bumped automatically. (2) An older ddflow meeting data written by a newer one writes what it understands and preserves everything it does not understand untouched (unknown keys, sections, fields, regions, event kinds); it is refused (exit 3, 'upgrade ddflow to >= X') only on a DIRECT CONFLICT: a write that would lose, overwrite or downgrade content a newer version wrote (e.g. re-rendering a managed file stamped by a newer ddflow, rewriting a config section in a newer format, minting ids under a scheme it cannot apply). (3) B-upgrade.2 manifest, .3 plan, .4 apply, .5 repairs, .6 notice and .7 end-to-end test are part of P-unify's finish line; .8-.11 stay after it. Research R-compat.

AMENDED 2026-10-17 (roadmap review contradictions; supersedes D-compat): LAYERING with D-upgrade-skew-guard (operator 2026-10-03): the two are not alternatives. The skew guard decides WHETHER an older ddflow may write at all (shipped default [upgrade].skew = refuse, once per session; an explicit --allow-older-version --reason override is recorded as skew.overridden). When the override or skew=warn lets it write, item (2) of this record governs WHAT it writes: it writes what it understands and preserves everything it does not, and is refused (exit 3) only on a DIRECT CONFLICT.
data.title: Compatibility: aliases until 1.0; older clones write what they understand and preserve the rest, refused only on a direct conflict; core of B-upgrade finishes with P-unify (amended 2026-10-17)

The same path-sco => PROPOSED: Single boundary: always-on files -> rules (B-rules-import); path-scoped files -> decision-with-globs by reference (B-path-rules-to-decisions) for the IMPORT side in every dialect (OB-rules-glob adds the dialect parsers to the rule_globs family and owns the EMIT side with the manifest). SDD-rules-bridge narrows to the Spec Kit constitution.md (one adapter-table row plus rules export into .specify/memory/constitution.md); Kiro steering import/export is done by OB-rules-glob and OB-agents-others (k

[medium] PL-native-export, SDD-export-tasks, PL-slice, PL-mirror: Three tasks write the same Kiro tasks.md: SDD-export-tasks (kiro flavour, region mode, checkbox state from task state), PL-native-export (.kiro/specs/ddflow-<label>/{requirements,design,tasks}.md) and PL-mirror (checkbox write-back). PL-slice and SDD-export-tasks both render a slice of queue tasks as a markdown checklist. D-sdd-plan-modes says native todo lists are mirrors and execution stays in the loop. => PROPOSED: One renderer (PL-slice projection + SDD-export-tasks formats). PL-native-export only decides WHERE a flavour is written per agent; PL-mirror's Kiro checkbox write-back is the existing export in region mode with ddflow owning the state (SDD-export-tasks), behind the knob, not a second writer.

[medium] SDD-model, OB-native-only, OB-model, D-ai-import, D-sdd-plan-modes: SDD-model defines a spec-source record kind (tool, path, digest, version, trust=imported) and OB-native-only lists 'Kiro specs, Spec Kit and OpenSpec trees' as pointer-plus-digest records (OB-model also gives trust=imported, origin digest and source path on every record). D-ai-import changed OB-native-only from pointer-only to managed. Research question 9 (does P-sdd absorb OB-native-only's Kiro/Spec Kit/OpenSpec items) was never answered in D-sdd-plan-modes. Result: two record kinds for the same tree, and a task title (OB-native-only: 'never emitted') that contradicts its own D-ai-import note => PROPOSED: SDD-model owns the spec-source kind; OB-native-only's spec-tree classes are instances of it (edge proposed). Retitle OB-native-only to 'Managed non-instruction classes: permissions and sandbox, hooks, plugins, output styles, off-disk team/org rules, auto memories (widening flag at plan review)' and remove the spec-tree classes from its list; SDD-import emits the records and the plan, OB-eval keeps the fixtures.

[high] B-org-trust, D-org-config: D-org-config (2) says a project's own config may declare company sources with NO machine allowlist, signatures optional; B-org-trust says 'a project cannot introduce a source the machine does not allow ... the allowlist lives in [REDACTED:path] or /etc/ddflow/org.toml, never in the project'. => PROPOSED: Follow the decision (operator 2026-10-06): the machine allowlist is optional and only restricts when present; safety comes from digest-approved executable content and the requirement of a valid signature for auto_apply = enforced. Rewrite the B-org-trust first sentence and tests; the 'cloned repo names an attacker's org' case is covered by inert-until-approved, not by an allowlist.

[high] B-review-convergence, D-failed-review-gate: B-review-convergence says complete and merge print a NOTE when not converged 'and NEVER block (D-failed-critic-not-blocking)'. D-failed-review-gate (operator 2026-10-17) makes merge and complete REFUSE a required review gate whose latest outcome is failed until confirmed findings are re-reviewed (fix rounds free). D-failed-critic-not-blocking is the earlier stance. => PROPOSED: Rewrite B-review-convergence: 'converged' reuses the D-failed-review-gate predicate in services/gates/outcomes.py (confirmed finding followed by a delta round that did not re-raise it) and the NOTE explains the refusal; the time-budget partial stays non-blocking only for the unreviewed-chunks case. Also its 'round n/max' must use the fix_round_free rule.

[medium] DX-watch-job, P-schedule.watch, DX-health-watch: Three tasks name the CLI noun `ddflow watch`: DX-watch-job (wait for a job/file/pid while renewing leases), P-schedule.watch (upstream-change watch records, declared/watch.py), and DX-health-watch's text (`ddflow watch inspect|status|history|ack`). The watchdog was in fact built as `ddflow health` (surfaces/declared/health.py). => PROPOSED: Keep `ddflow watch` for P-schedule.watch (a record kind with add/edit verbs, D-schedule-early) ; DX-watch-job becomes `ddflow wait --job/--file/--pid/--gate` (its own text says reuse ddflow wait) or `ddflow job watch`; fix the stale CLI name in DX-health-watch's body and DX-health-watch-liveness.

[high] DX-dispatch-supervise, DX-health-watch, D-lease-break-explicit: Two ladders. DX-health-watch's CORRECT ladder is nudge -> ask status -> request yield -> park -> take over/relaunch -> escalate, with act|advise modes; DX-dispatch-supervise (amended 2026-10-15 to consume the watchdog) still lists 'nudge the lane, request yield, take over, relaunch' and its own stall = no progress watermark for [dispatch].stall_s while another item waits. It also takes over with 'recover and claim --force', but D-lease-break-explicit made the sanctioned break `ddflow claim --break` (break_on_timeout default false). => PROPOSED: One owner per step: the watchdog owns detection and the nudge/yield/park/escalate ladder (and [watch].act); DX-dispatch-supervise owns only refill-after-merge, RESUME/relaunch (via DX-park-and-resume) and merge order, and uses `claim --break` for take-over only when policy allows. Delete [dispatch].stall_s in favour of [watch].stall_s.

[medium] DX-dispatch-launch, DM-kinds, D-daemons: D-daemons (1) lists five kinds ddflow may start: scheduler tick, watchers, serve, hub mirror, lane supervisor. DM-kinds ships scheduler tick, serve, hub mirror, watchers and omits the lane supervisor; DX-dispatch-launch ships ddflow/templates/daemons/lane-supervisor.toml before the daemon record kind exists. DM-kinds also ships a hub mirror kind while KB-mirror (prio 64) does not exist. => PROPOSED: DM-kinds owns the template files for kinds whose command exists: scheduler tick, watchers, serve, lane supervisor (calling DX-dispatch-launch's tick). The hub-mirror kind template moves to KB-mirror (add a need KB-mirror -> DM-kinds).

[medium] P-agent-parity.launcher, DM-lifecycle, DM-supervisors, CP-backend-iface, P-spawn.engine: 'One supervisor, not three': the launcher is a detached supervisor over `ddflow job run`; DM-lifecycle/DM-supervisors define a pidfile + backoff supervisor with its own adapter interface (start, stop, status, logs; child process, systemd, launchd, tmux, container); CP-backend-iface defines a lane backend interface (start, steer, report, stop, status; process, tmux, paseo, opencode, orca, acp) and CP-backend-tmux is needed by DM-supervisors. Two registries and two tmux adapters. => PROPOSED: Single process layer: jobs engine + launcher 'process' backend. CP-backend-iface is the one registry; a daemon is a long-lived lane of kind=daemon whose adapter set is a subset (start, stop, status, logs); DM-supervisors then only adds the systemd/launchd unit emitters (consent) and DM-lifecycle only the pidfile lock, restart cap 3 and policy (D-daemons). Add needs DM-lifecycle -> P-agent-parity.launcher and DM-supervisors -> CP-backend-iface (already transitive through CP-backend-tmux).

[medium] P-safeguards.dispatch, DX-dispatch-plan, DX-agent-brief, P-spawn.context, B-gap-lanes: Four brief renderers for one purpose: `ddflow lanes brief` (done), `ddflow brief --for-agent` (DX-agent-brief, done), `ddflow dispatch brief <item> --role` (P-safeguards.dispatch, same command noun and files as DX-dispatch-plan), and the dispatch brief of P-spawn.context (services/lanes/brief.py). => PROPOSED: services/agent_brief.py is the renderer; P-safeguards.dispatch adds the role/safeguards/envelope sections to it (and the `dispatch brief` subcommand under DX-dispatch-plan's package); P-spawn.context and the planner call it; services/lanes/brief.py stays the ledger view.

[medium] P-schedule.unattended, DX-dispatch-launch, P-schedule.executor-basic, D-dispatch-modes: Two owners for 'start headless lanes for ready items within caps when nobody is there': P-schedule.unattended (executor + lane launcher + caps + quota guard) and DX-dispatch-launch (mode launch, tick, caps, guards, operator-only). D-dispatch-modes also requires a kill switch and schedule.max_parallel_tasks as the cap; DX-dispatch-launch mentions neither. => PROPOSED: DX-dispatch-launch owns the tick that starts lanes; P-schedule.unattended only registers/emits an executor that runs it and detects the silent no-fire. Add 'kill switch ([dispatch].enabled / `ddflow dispatch off`) and schedule.max_parallel_tasks cap' to DX-dispatch-launch's acceptance.

[high] GV-kimi-reviewer, D-kimi, GV-kimi-models: D-kimi (5) records that the operator asked for the Kimi reviewer immediately and that GV-kimi-reviewer 'is moved up'; the task sits at prio 50 behind GV-kimi-models -> P-governor.model-registry -> B-ac-smoke/B-sub-model and GV-capabilities. A kimi-k3 reviewer entry (family moonshot, gates empty) is already in the local reviewers.toml and the family is in config_sections/agent.py, so part of the task is probably done operationally; DX-reviewer-failover came out of the Kimi 5-hour quota running out. => PROPOSED: Drop the GV-kimi-models edge, prio 33; reduce the task to: moonshot in reviewers detect, sensitivity gate before sending the diff, unavailable-not-passed on a missing key/endpoint, and the failover list (DX-reviewer-failover). Verify what the existing entry already covers before building.

[medium] B-lease-edit-only-hold, D-lease-break-explicit, D-lease-hold-limit: B-lease-edit-only-hold (prio 100) still specifies break_on_timeout default true and says the claim logic is unbuilt; D-lease-break-explicit set the default false (explicit `claim --break`) and DX-lease-progress-breakable (done) built hold_max_s/break_on_timeout in config_sections/lease.py and the break. Its part (c) merge reconciliation is unbuilt (grep: no merge.reconciled/reconcile_tests). => PROPOSED: Narrow it to lease.overlap events, `ddflow lease break|keep` surfaces and the briefs; fold (c) into B-lease-reconcile-merge; update the break_on_timeout default; order after B-lease-hold-visibility as today.

[low] FL-roster, FL-surfaces: FL-roster declares `ddflow agents list|show|set` on every surface itself; FL-surfaces ('ddflow fleet|fanout|agents|receipt') is the task that declares those commands (ddflow/surfaces/declared/fleet*.py). Two owners of the `agents` verb. => PROPOSED: FL-roster ships the record kind and service (RC1-RC12) only; FL-surfaces declares `agents`. Also check the `agents` noun against P-subagents' `ddflow agent` commands before declaring.

[medium] B-upstream-detectors, B-trigger-events: Both add an uncaught-exception capture: B-upstream-detectors puts catch-alls in cli.main / MCP serve that classify an internal exception and store a last-failure record; B-trigger-events adds 'crash/exception report (ddflow report crash + hook for uncaught tracebacks, ties B-upstream-detectors)'. => PROPOSED: B-upstream-detectors owns the classifier and the last-failure record and emits one crash event kind; B-trigger-events only registers that event as a trigger source (no second hook, no `ddflow report crash`).

[medium] DX-phase-review, D-phase-review, GV-roles, P-governor.tier-suggest: D-phase-review uses `tier:fast` as a RISK/depth label for per-item review (one combined round); the same tag is the governor's model-tier hint (tier:fast|balanced|deep, advisory, set by P-governor.tier-suggest and moved by the governor ladder). Also GV-roles says planner 'strong', while D-governor fixed the names fast|balanced|deep. A model-tier downshift at 40-60 % quota would silently turn on single-round review. => PROPOSED: Use a separate review-depth label/knob (e.g. risk:low or [review].depth by glob) not derived from the model tier, or state in DX-phase-review that review depth reads only a human-set tier tag, never the governor's effective tier (GV-guardrails: floors never relaxed). Use the registry tier names fast|balanced|deep in GV-roles.

[medium] B-sched-due, B-sched-run, P-schedule.executor-basic, P-schedule.unattended, P-schedule.chain, P-schedule.outcomes, D-schedule-early: D-schedule-early governs ddflow/services/schedule/** (a package) and P-schedule.executor-basic/unattended/chain/outcomes create ddflow/services/schedule/executor.py, chain.py, history.py, while B-sched-due/-run/-defaults/-escalation edit the module ddflow/services/schedule.py. A package directory shadows the module of the same name; B-sched-emitters already chose a flat name (services/schedule_emit.py). P-schedule.executor-basic and P-schedule.unattended also both claim executor.py and surfaces/declared/schedule.py. => PROPOSED: Either make the first schedule task (B-sched-due, prio 15) convert schedule.py into the package with a facade and have the later ones use it, or use flat names (schedule_executor.py, schedule_chain.py, schedule_history.py). P-schedule.unattended should extend executor-basic's module, not redefine it.

[low] B-sched-compaction, P-lessons.curate, B-coh-sweep: B-sched-compaction (weekly job: find lessons, instructions, tasks, bugs that are duplicated/contradictory/closable) and P-lessons.curate (a lessons pass that verifies, deduplicates, retires stale ones, proposes merges) overlap on lessons; both sit on the retroactive coherence sweep (B-coh-sweep). => PROPOSED: P-lessons.curate is the lessons-specific candidate generator and report; B-sched-compaction is the scheduling wrapper over B-coh-sweep and P-lessons.curate output for lessons (add a need B-sched-compaction -> P-lessons.curate when planned).

[medium] DX-dispatch-launch, D-dispatch-modes: D-dispatch-modes requires a kill switch and schedule.max_parallel_tasks as the cap; DX-dispatch-launch/-plan do not mention a kill switch; D-dispatch-modes governs ddflow/services/dispatch/** but the tasks' globs are flat modules. => PROPOSED: Add a kill-switch knob and command to DX-dispatch-launch and the package globs (see narrow_globs).

[medium] TF-record, TD-import-core: JUnit XML ingest is in both: TF-record ('JUnit XML ingest, summary plus hash, repeats, seed, SUT pin') and TD-import-core ('Importers: JUnit XML, Cucumber, Robot ... registry adapters'). TD-import-core needs TF-record, so it must not re-implement JUnit. => PROPOSED: TF-record owns the record shape and the JUnit reader as the first row; TD-import-core registers it in the importer registry and adds Cucumber, Robot and per-scenario importers only; say so in both bodies.

[medium] SC-style-codeguide, P-safeguards.style-cards: SC-style-codeguide's title says 'style cards derived from the project's own tool configs found by the probe'; that is the deliverable of P-safeguards.style-cards ([tool.ruff] etc. to a committed card per language). SC-style-codeguide's body says it only feeds the cards and the consult action. => PROPOSED: Limit SC-style-codeguide to proposing which codeguide languages and context7 libraries to enable from the stack profile and registering them for the consult action; the cards stay with P-safeguards.style-cards. Retitle.

[medium] AI-lifecycle, CN-roles, CN-cr: AI-lifecycle plans 'a deprecated module version notifies its consumers with a deadline'; CN-roles records 'a deprecation window unless waived' and CN-cr is the consumer-notification record with per-consumer burndown. Two notification paths for the same event. => PROPOSED: A deprecation notice is a change request of kind deprecation (deadline = the window), delivered by CN-cr/CN-states; AI-lifecycle adds only the app-infra triggers (decommission, secret rotation by reference) and the destroy-plan approval.

[medium] B-lease-edit-only-hold, DX-lease-progress-breakable: B-lease-edit-only-hold (D-lease-hold-limit) is still open with the full design: [lease].hold_max_s, break_on_timeout, reconcile_tests, lease.overlap, `lease break/keep`. DX-lease-progress-breakable (DONE) already shipped hold_max_s, idle_max_s and break_on_timeout in config_sections/lease.py and a claim --break that records lease.expired and keeps the holder's branch (verified in the code). B-lease-edit-only-hold's model differs: the waiter's claim goes through with BOTH leases live (lease.overlap) and a full reconcile test run at merge, versus the shipped one-holder-breaks model. => PROPOSED: Rewrite B-lease-edit-only-hold to the part not built (reconcile_tests after a merge over another item's files, `lease keep --for N`, operator `lease break`) or abandon it in favour of DX-park-and-resume (restore) plus DX-lease-yield-doctor-status; decide which model stands by an operator decision. Its needs include the done P-unify and B-lease-hold-visibility.

[medium] DX-dispatch-launch, P-agent-parity.launcher, P-agent-parity.continuation, CP-backend-iface: DX-dispatch-launch (priority 55, tagged feature/dispatch) needs three feature tasks (P-agent-parity.launcher, P-agent-parity.continuation, CP-backend-iface). The rule 'DX-*/fix-* tasks never need a feature' is violated, and a DX id at 55 is mis-banded. The other DX-dispatch-* tasks (plan, nudge, supervise, acceptance) correctly stay in the DX band and do not depend on it. => PROPOSED: Keep the edges (they are real prerequisites) but re-file the task outside the DX namespace (e.g. P-agent-parity.dispatch-launch, same body and needs) and abandon DX-dispatch-launch as a rename; do not make DX-dispatch-acceptance need it (it does not today).

[medium] RH-place-unphased, DX-default-priority-for-dx, D-old-work-behind-core-docs-accepted: RH-place-unphased says to move fix-test-duration-* and fix-ci-split-slow-tests into a new P-test-speed phase, but its own 2026-10-16 STALE NOTE says fix/DX tasks keep their own track and need no phase, and D-old-work-behind-core-docs says any fix- item carries no hold (a new phase would inherit phase needs and hold them). P-test-robustness (12 tasks) already exists for test economy. Its list also names done tasks (B-log-snapshot-knobs). => PROPOSED: Do NOT create P-test-speed or move fix-* tasks. Reduce RH-place-unphased to the non-fix, non-DX unphased open tasks (recount below).

Seen 2026-10-17 (RH-contradictions-2026-10-17): 'ddflow --json show B-lease-edit-only-hold' returned a refusal 'no such item or bug' once, and the same call succeeded seconds later (concurrent writers). Wanted: a read never reports a missing item because of a half-folded or rebuilding index; retry or read the log. Regression test: a reader racing a writer never sees a refusal for an existing id.
